messages:
incident-bot: [PAGE] high error rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (severity: P2) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Alert details: 5xx spike from 13:55-14:03, rate 18% -> 42%. Suspected routing imbalance. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-914
Alex: saw the bot, jumping in. I can confirm increased 502/504s in the gateway metrics.
Alex: initial guess: autoscaler hit a weird failure and one of the regional routing pools got incorrectly marked unhealthy.
Priya: on my way. I'm primed for routing / LB checks. assigning myself secondary for this page. @Alex you're primary?
Alex: yea I'm primary. Priya is secondary. @Taylor I'll need you for any quick capacity bumps if we need to spin pools.
Taylor: available, watching.
Mike: FYI I already saw a handful of customer reports in Intercom for timeouts around 13:58. Customer impact looks partial (some requests succeed).
Sara: digging into logs -> partial 502s from the inference proxy, error is "upstream read timeout". Sample log:
```
2026-06-03T13:59:12Z proxy-01 us-west-2 inference-proxy ERROR upstream read timeout id=ab12 status=502 target=nv-rt-03
```
Alex: that matches. Two threads: 1) routing is misdirecting too much traffic to nv-rt-03 which is slow, 2) autoscaler didn't evict it.
devops-bot: Autoscaler attempted scale down on nv-rt-03 at 13:45, saw oom/killer events and flagged node unhealthy: events: [OOMKilled, DiskPressure]. Node was not cordoned due to transient API error.
Priya: ok plan: 1) remove nv-rt-03 from routing (soft drain) 2) enable fallback pool us-west-2-burst 3) temporarily increase routing weight to us-east-1 for low-latency customers 4) watch errors for 15m.
Alex: doing step 1 now. Runbook link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/routing-fallbacks
Alex: ```kubectl label node nv-rt-03 maintenance=true && curl -XPOST https://internal-router/redwood/drain?node=nv-rt-03```
Alex: done. nv-rt-03 marked draining, routing reduced by 78% in 30s.
Taylor: I enabled us-west-2-burst pool and increased capacity +10% as a short-term buffer.
devops-bot: Burst pool spin-up completed at 14:12. All new instances passed health checks.
Priya: monitoring: error rate dropped from 42% -> 8% over 10 minutes. Latency percentile improved.
Mike: customer reports still trickling but new ones are low severity. Notifying customer success to update status page.
Sara: keeping an eye on KV cache hit rates — small degradation while routing weight shifted, but no evictions.
Alex: current status: degraded -> partial service impairment for ~18 minutes, now mostly mitigated. Primary/secondary for remainder of the shift: Alex primary (until 18:00), Priya secondary. Taylor on-call for capacity changes.
Priya: next steps before handoff: 1) schedule a reimage for nv-rt-03 (disk/oom root cause) 2) run A/B regression checks for model quality after routing change 3) follow-up postmortem if root cause confirmed.
Taylor: I'll own the reimage and put a doc in hw-ops with steps + ETA.
Mike: CS update drafted and posted to status.redwood.ai. Linking: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-06-03-routing-spike
Alex: Runbook pointers in summary: - routing-fallbacks runbook above - autoscaler health checks: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/autoscaler - logging query to reproduce sample: `service:proxy error:upstream read timeout`
Priya: handoff note for night team: watch for recurring OOM events in nv-rt-* over the next 24h. If OOM repeat, escalate to infra-eng.
Alex: Okay handing off at 18:00 to @Taylor (night primary) and @Sara (night secondary). Items for handoff: reimage ticket, postmortem owner (Priya), follow-up on autoscaler API flakiness (Alex).
Taylor: ack, will pick up at 18:00.
Priya: ack, I'll own postmortem and add timeline + RCA once nv-rt-03 reimaged.
incident-bot: Incident auto-close candidate: metrics stable for 30m, propose to close at 14:45 if no regressions.
Alex: leaving thread open until reimage scheduled. Marking status: mitigated but not resolved. :white_check_mark:
Sara: thanks team — good quick coordination. I'll keep a watch window till 15:00 then pass to oncall rotation.
